info.title: Frappé API
info.description: The operating system for restaurants and cafés in Latin America. Version 1 is anonymous and rate limited per client; its administration writes are not authenticated yet. Texts follow Accept-Language and Content-Language names the languages served; every endpoint declares its caching, and cacheable answers carry strong ETags; every error is an RFC 9457 Problem Details with a stable code.

get.description: Every ISO 3166-1 country, ordered by code, with its codes, its name and its currencies in use. Names answer in the language of Accept-Language: the requested tag, then its base language, any Portuguese in pt-BR, then English. Content-Language names the languages served.

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description: The languages the client accepts (BCP 47, with q weights). Frappé is written in en, es, es-AR, es-MX, pt-BR; the ranges are tried from the highest quality down and the first one served wins (fr, es-AR;q=0.8 answers in es-AR). Another Spanish answers in es, any Portuguese in pt-BR, and anything else, or no header, in English. Content-Language names the language served.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: ETags of the copies the client holds (or *): when one matches, the answer is 304 without a body.

Content-Language.description: The languages Frappé's own texts in the response are written in; absent when it holds none, only proper nouns, identifiers and source data (names and categories as their source publishes them).

ETag.description: Strong validator of this representation, language included; send it back in If-None-Match.

Cache-Control.description: public, max-age=86400 at most (seconds); some answers expire sooner, such as time zones before an offset change.

Vary.description: Accept-Language: each language is a separate representation with its own ETag; a cache keys on it.

Content-Language.description: The languages the problem's texts are written in.

get.summary: A date in a country's business calendar
get.description: Whether a date (YYYY-MM-DD) is a business day in a country under a policy, its kind and its observances. policy (required) is banking (settlements and payments), labor (payroll: read kind, the day's strongest observance) or commercial (suppliers and deadlines). Each country declares what its policies close: its weekend, the kinds of observance and the sector calendars each policy treats as non-working; GET /v1/geo/countries/{code} lists the policies it answers and its time zone. 404 geo.holidays.not_covered when Geo lacks a calendar the answer needs, geo.business_days.not_covered when the country has no rules for the policy; each answer names the general calendars it read (covers) and credits the sources of every calendar read (attributions), as their terms ask. A missing parameter is 400 geo.parameter.required.

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description: The languages the client accepts (BCP 47, with q weights). Frappé is written in en, es, es-AR, es-MX, pt-BR; the ranges are tried from the highest quality down and the first one served wins (fr, es-AR;q=0.8 answers in es-AR). Another Spanish answers in es, any Portuguese in pt-BR, and anything else, or no header, in English. Content-Language names the language served.

AddressResponse.description:
A validated, normalized address: the snapshot the client's module stores as its own copy (Geo stores none), with the
reference that re-validates it later. The ISO codes are null when Geo could not map them.

AddressSuggestionListResponse.description: The suggestions for what the user typed so far, best first.

AddressSuggestionResponse.description: A suggestion: its opaque id (validate it with POST address-validations), its full text, and its main and secondary parts.

AddressValidationRequest.description:
The address to validate: a suggestion's Reference (its `id`) or one kept with a snapshot, the
search Session it closes, and optionally the Language of the answer (BCP 47,
else `Accept-Language`).

AreaListResponse.description: A subdivision's administrative areas, ordered by level then name.

AreaResponse.description: An administrative area below the first level: its level (2, 3, ...), its category as the source writes it, and whether it is a local government.

AttributionResponse.description: A source to credit: its name, a working link to it and its license, when it names one.

BusinessDayResponse.description:
A date in a jurisdiction under a policy. `businessDay` answers the policy; `kind` is the day's strongest
observance (`holiday`, `tourist_non_working_day`, `non_working_day`, `community_non_working_day`;
null for an ordinary day), which is what payroll (`labor`) needs; `observances` are those the policy looked
at; `covers` names the general calendars read; `attributions` credits the sources of every calendar read, as
their terms ask: show it wherever the observances are shown.

BusinessDaysResponse.description:
The next business days in a jurisdiction under a policy, from `from` (included), in order. `covers` names
the general calendars read; `attributions` credits the sources of every calendar read, as their terms ask: show
it wherever these dates are shown.

CentroidResponse.description: A representative point (WGS 84) published by the source.

CountryDetailResponse.description: One country, as CountryResponse, with what Geo covers for it (CapabilitiesResponse).

CountryResponse.description: A country: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, alpha-3 and numeric codes, its name, and its currencies in order of preference.

CurrencyResponse.description: A currency: ISO 4217 code, CLDR name and standard symbol (same language), and its minor unit digits.

HolidayCalendarResponse.description:
The observances that apply in a jurisdiction in a year, by date. `covers` names the calendars they come from:
the country's, then the subdivision's own when Geo has it. `attributions` credits the sources of those
calendars, as their terms ask: show it wherever the observances are shown. `scope` is the calendars' scope
(`general`, or a sector's such as `banking`, which lists its source's facts as published).

HolidayCoverageResponse.description: The years Geo holds a country's calendar of one scope for, in order.

HolidaySyncRequestResponse.description:
A run asked for by hand: the request's id (`requestId`; requests made before the Worker starts are run once, so
it is not a run's id), the source, and when it was asked for. The run appears among the source's runs (Location)
once the Worker ran it.

HolidaySyncResponse.description:
A holiday source: when it last ran (`lastAttemptAt`), how that ended (`lastOutcome`: `applied`,
`unchanged`, `not_published`, `refused` or `failed`) and when it last succeeded.

LegalBasisRequest.description:
The norm of an observance set by hand: `citation` (required when a basis is given, up to 200 characters) and
`url`, the absolute `http` or `https` address of its text (up to 500 characters). Strings, so a value
that is not an address is answered with a Geo error instead of a binding failure.

LegalBasisResponse.description: The norm that establishes an observance (`citation`), and the address of its text (`url`) when known.

LocalityPageResponse.description: One page of localities; string? LocalityPageResponse.NextCursor asks for the next one and is absent on the last page.

LocalityResponse.description: A populated place, with the ids of its level-2 area and of its local government when the source knows them.

ObservanceOverrideRequest.description:
An observance set by hand: `date` (`yyyy-MM-dd`) and `name` identify it; `kind` is
`holiday`, `tourist_non_working_day`, `non_working_day` or `community_non_working_day` (which
needs `community`, one the country declares); `movedFrom` is the original date of a moved holiday. Date, name
and kind are required; the rest are optional.

ObservanceResponse.description:
One reason a date is not an ordinary day. `kind` is `holiday`, `tourist_non_working_day`,
`non_working_day` or `community_non_working_day` (with its `community`); `movedFrom` is the
original date of a moved holiday; `legalBasis` cites its norm and links its text (`url`) when known.

ObservanceSuppressionRequest.description: The source's observance to leave out: its `date` (`yyyy-MM-dd`) and `name`.

OverrideConflictResponse.description: An observance (by date and name) of a jurisdiction's year whose manual override won over a change of the source.

examples.title: The resource does not exist.
examples.detail: The URL does not match any endpoint of the API.

errors.message: The URL does not match any endpoint of the API.

type.description: The category of the failure: urn:frappe:problem: and a stable slug. It never names an error code.

title.description: Stable summary of the category, in the language of Content-Language.

detail.description: The error's text when there is one, or how many errors there are, in the language of Content-Language.

errors.description: Every error found, so a client can fix them all at once.

traceId.description: W3C trace id of the request, to find it in the logs and traces.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 Problem Details. type is the category of the failure; the error codes are only in errors, which always lists every error, one or several.

parameters.description: The values the error was raised with, by name (the same the texts use).

message.description: The error in the language of Content-Language; absent when no text exists.

ProblemError.description: One error: its stable code, the values it was raised with and its text in the response language.

SubdivisionAliasListResponse.description: A subdivision's aliases, the source's and the manual ones, by alias.

SubdivisionAliasRequest.description: Another name a subdivision is known by, up to 200 characters.

SubdivisionAliasResponse.description: An alias of a subdivision and its `origin`: `source` (the territory sync keeps it) or `manual` (added by hand).

SubdivisionListResponse.description: A country's first-level subdivisions, ordered by code.

SubdivisionResponse.description: A first-level subdivision: ISO 3166-2 code, its country, name and category as the source writes them, and other names it is known by.

SyncRunListResponse.description: A source's latest runs, newest first.

SyncRunResponse.description:
One audited run: its outcome, the calendars it opened (`inserted`) and changed (`updated`), why it failed
or was refused (`error`), and the manual overrides the source changed something under (`conflicts`).
